summary: Tenant-aware batching cohort shrinkage causing intermittent p95/p99 flush delays
description: Issue summary: LexaHealth reported intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and request timeouts during sustained medium QPS (40-70 qps) on their Dedicated pool. Spikes correlate with short windows when tenant cohort sizes shrink below typical batching thresholds, producing delayed flushes and occasional 504 timeouts for short streams. Impact: customer-facing latency degradations causing application errors and user-visible failures. Environment: Dedicated pool (lexa-dedicated-01), prod us-west region, serving runtime 2.14.3, continuous-batcher tuned with tenant-aware weighting.
impact: Intermittent p95/p99 latency increases up to 2.8s (baseline p95 ~350ms) and periodic 504 timeouts affecting ~0.6% of requests during observed windows. Customer reports failed checkout flows in production during three 10-15 minute windows over the past 24h.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate LexaHealth traffic profile: sustained 40-70 qps with a mix of short (avg 12 tokens) and long streams. 2) Target requests to Dedicated pool lexadp-usw2 with tenant-aware batching enabled. 3) Observe batcher metrics: cohort_size_by_tenant, batch_flush_latency_ms, and request_timeouts. 4) Reproduce by introducing transient tenant weight change (simulate tenant reweighting event or shard movement).
logs: Relevant traces: trace-id 0b7f9c2a produced a 504 at 2026-03-10T18:14:22Z. Sample stack: continuous-batcher flushing loop -> cohort-aggregator wait_for_flush() -> schedule_flush(). Grafana panel: /d/redwood/batcher#cohort_flush_latency shows sawtooth spikes aligned with tenant weight adjustments. Error snippet: "flush timeout after 1500ms (cohort_size=1)". Router logs show fallbacks to smaller model variants during spikes.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: batcher timer drift. Ruled out: no clock skew on nodes; timers stable.
- Observed correlation between tenant-reweight events (internal autoscaler activity) and cohort size collapse: when tenant weight changes, continuous-batcher moves requests to new cohorts; during handoff small partial cohorts wait full linger window before flush.
- Telemetry shows flush latency increases only for cohorts with size < configured min_cohort_size=4 and when tenant's weighting rebalancer runs.
- KV cache warmup and model load times were normal; GPU utilization remained moderate (~48%).
- Reproduced in staging by toggling tenant weight; reproduction required mixing short-stream-heavy traffic and weight change frequency >1/min.

comments: Maya Chen (support): Customer saw three distinct windows with visible failures. Asking for escalation to runtime team.
Diego Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed correlation with tenant_reweight events in lexadp autoscaler logs. Prioritized as P1 due to customer impact.

Priya Nair (runtime): Reproduced in staging. Small cohorts created during handoff were waiting full linger interval; will prototype skipping linger for cohorts created as part of handoff. Related PR planned.
CS update to customer: We have a mitigation rolling that reduces min cohort linger for your pool; monitoring for improvement.
root_cause: Cohort handoff path in the continuous-batcher does not bypass the standard linger timer. When the tenant reweighting / shard movement creates a new cohort, short requests can fall into newly-created cohorts smaller than the expected aggregation size and then wait for the full linger window, producing p95/p99 spikes and occasional timeouts.
workaround: Applied temporary config on lexadp-usw2: tenant_batch_min_size lowered from 4 -> 2 and cohort_creation_skip_linger=true for the affected tenant. This reduced observed p99 latency and eliminated new 504s during mitigation window.
resolution: In progress. Runtime team has an in-development patch that tags cohorts created by reweight/handoff and forces immediate flush or aggressive linger bypass for cohorts with short-sequence traffic. Patch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4382. Planning staged rollout: canary on lexadp-usw2, followed by full pool rollout if stable. Post-mitigation monitoring planned for 72h.
follow_up_actions: Merge and ship PR 4382; run canary on lexadp-usw2 (owner: Priya Nair).
Add unit/integration tests for cohort handoff path to ensure linger bypass behavior (owner: runtime QA).
Create a postmortem doc in Confluence describing root cause and long-term fix options; include perf comparison of bypass vs normal linger (owner: Diego Alvarez).
Evaluate if default tenant_batch_min_size should be lowered or if reweight operations should be rate-limited in Dedicated pools to reduce churn.
